1) Situation Summary: Competitor launched a quarter-limited "founding customers" promo that Sales cites in live deals and our win rate vs. that bundle has fallen from ~55% to ~35%; Finance warns broad outcome-pricing or heavy discounts could compress gross margin 4–6 pts—board wants a decisive response that preserves margin and meets imminent promo pressure.

4) Recommended Portfolio of Moves (3–4 moves with pricing/margin guardrails): i) Immediate War Room (0–7d) to triage deals and approve up to 8 founders-match revenue-share deals (max total exposure = X% of quarterly ARR, CFO must sign off) to stop near-term losses; ii) Deploy 60-day Outcome POC to top 20 accounts within 30–60d (max 15% gross-price concession, rebates ≤5% in escrow, success metric = lift win-rate to ≥50% vs bundle); iii) Launch 90–180d hyperscaler co-sell pilot on a revenue-share basis with a floor gross-margin requirement (set target floor at company median margin −2 pts) to avoid >2 pts structural erosion; iv) Fund a 6–9mo replatform (modular AI runtime + compliance features) by sunsetting two low-margin SKUs (CTO+Product+CFO ownership).  
5) Risk & Contingency Plan: Triggers—if post-pilot win-rate vs bundle <50% by day 90, then (A) expand targeted revenue-share offers to selected verticals with CFO approval, (B) pause new outcome SLAs and shift to time-and-materials + capped rebates while SWAT delivery team stabilizes performance, (C) accelerate SKU bundling or pursue tuck-in acquisition of an AI-native stack; AI transparency mitigation = Legal sign-off gate before any customer-facing AI feature, mandatory audit logs, configurable explainability, and a product toggle to disable automated actions per-account.  
6) Execution Milestones (owners & timelines): War Room live 0–7d (CEO sponsor); select 8 founders-match deals + start 60-day Outcome POCs by day 30 (CRO + Solutions Eng + CFO); hyperscaler pilot contracts signed by day 90 and live 90–180d (Partnerships + Sales); replatform funded by SKU sunset decision within 120d, MVP 6–9mo (CTO + Product); report back to board with 90d checkpoint metrics (win-rate vs bundle, margin delta, POC conversion).

1) Situation Summary: Competitor extended the founding-promo for another quarter, creating sustained price pressure; our war-room cohort win-rate improved to 42% but with ~1.5pt margin erosion vs. baseline, and the regulator’s draft now requires explainability/logging/customer controls inside 9–12 months—so we must both defend share immediately and be reg-ready within 9–12 months.  
2) Market & Competitor Snapshot: The extended promo entrenches price sensitivity in high-velocity deals while the competitor’s vague “enterprise controls” roadmap defers a reg-ready answer, making rapid compliance a commercial differentiator we can exploit.  
3) Strategic Options: A) Limited founders‑match revenue‑share (primary metric: 90‑day win rate) — cap to ≤10 deals to arrest churn; B) Compliance‑by‑Design fast‑track (primary metric: 12‑month margin + regulatory readiness) — build audit logs, explainability endpoints, per‑account toggles in 90–120d; C) 60‑day Outcome POCs with escrowed rebates (primary metrics: 90‑day win rate & POC conversion) — top‑20 accounts, max 15% concession, ≤5% escrow; D) Hyperscaler co‑sell revenue‑share pilot (primary metric: 12‑month win rate and margin recovery) — revenue‑share with margin floor.  
4) Recommended Portfolio of Moves (targets, base & downside impacts): (i) War room + ≤10 revenue‑share matches + top‑20 60‑day POCs — target win rate vs bundle ≥50% at 90d (base) and ≥60% at 12 months (base); margin impact = ~1.5pt compression at 90d (base), downside up to 3.5–4.0pts if matches scale without caps, and at 12 months expect net impact ≤1.0pt (base) and worst‑case ≤2.0pts after compliance + hyperscaler effects reduce concession needs; (ii) Compliance‑by‑Design (90–120d) — reduces required concessions and is estimated to shave ~1.0pt off 12‑month downside vs no compliance; (iii) Hyperscaler pilot (90–180d) — enforces a margin floor (company median −2pts) to limit structural erosion and aid 12‑month recovery.  
5) Risk & Contingency Plan (base vs downside triggers and concise responses): Base = win‑rate ≥50% at 90d with ~1.5pt margin drag; Triggers & responses: if win‑rate <50% at 90d → narrow founders‑match to 3–5 vertical proof points and shift new deals to T&M + capped rebates; if margin erosion >2.0pts → pause new outcome SLAs, halt scaling of matches, accelerate SKU sunset or pursue selective tuck‑in M&A for AI‑native capability; AI transparency controls = mandatory Legal sign‑off gate, per‑account toggles, audit logs and explainability endpoints before any matched deal.  
6) Execution Milestones (owners & time buckets): 0–30d = war room live, select matches, begin 60‑day POCs (CEO sponsor; CRO, Solutions Eng, CFO); 30–90d = complete POCs, ship 2‑SKU compliance changes (CRO, Solutions Eng, CTO/Product); 90–180d = hyperscaler pilot live and platform MVP planning (Partnerships, Product); 12–18 months = scale platform/marketplace and achieve reg‑ready posture (CTO, Product, CFO); 90‑day board checkpoint to validate win‑rate and margin metrics and trigger contingencies.

overall_validity.rationale: Key variables and rules are instantiated faithfully: the manager provides a highly prescriptive template while repeatedly emphasizing unconventional strategy (innovation-first), the assistant has shared but non-final authority, and consequences depend on instruction-following and plan quality with only mild evaluative penalties and no extra reward for initiative. The environment shows high disruption and urgent timelines via repeated competitor and regulatory shocks and a pulled-forward board review; resources are consistently partial but periodically updated with specific data (finance decks, win/loss cuts, feasibility notes). Actor behavior matches a directive-mixed manager who enforces structure but invites bold ideas, and all consequences are framed as scores and feedback without structural changes to role or incentives. Rendering adheres to the requested realism (no meta, event-centric, tightly matched across rounds). Minor deviations (e.g., slightly more frequent resource updates than specified, compliance strictness at the stricter end of ‘moderate’) are subtle and do not meaningfully distort the causal structure relevant to the tested behavior, so their impact on the results is peripheral.
